slides.text: My daughter Lily vanished seven years ago from her ground-floor bedroom. The police found no forced entry, no DNA, no footprints. The case went ice cold. Yesterday, while renovating our basement, I smashed open a hollow section of drywall and found a dusty Polaroid camera hidden inside. My hands shook as I pushed the eject button. A single, undeveloped photo slid out. I waited in agonizing silence as the image slowly came to life.

It was Lily. She looked exactly as she did the night she disappeared, wearing her yellow pajamas. But she wasn't dead. She was asleep, curled up on a dirty mattress. My heart soared with a desperate, frantic hope until I looked closer at the background of the photograph. The distinct floral wallpaper... the cracked wooden baseboard... the dripping copper pipe. I recognized the room immediately. It was my own basement.

A floorboard creaked above me. My husband, David, was supposed to be at work. We had lived in this house for ten years. I flipped the Polaroid over. On the back, in David's unmistakable handwriting, was a date: Last Tuesday. My blood turned to ice. The heavy basement door at the top of the stairs suddenly clicked shut, and the deadbolt locked from the outside. 'I told you not to dig down there, honey,' David whispered.
